archetype: Warrior-group melee bruiser that spends HP instead of MP and derives its damage range from Max HP rather than STR. Sustained-damage profile built around the Exceed/Overload cycle plus Nether Shield, with heavy self-sustain from Life Sap.

mechanics.claim: HEXA Enhancement final damage rises linearly per level with jumps at levels 10, 20 and 30, and Enhancements require the matching V skill to be maxed and equipped. Verbatim: 'Enhancements require the corresponding V Skill to be leveled to max and equipped. Final Damage bonuses from Enhancements increase linearly each level, with a jump at levels 10, 20, and 30.' The four Demon Avenger enhancement formulas on the skills page all read 10+x+5*log10(x)+5*log20(x)+10*log30(x), which is exactly that shape.

PROVENANCE WARNING, re-confirmed 2026-09-12 by opening the image: the 'Energy Efficient' image carries a Korean checkbox header (본인 스펙 추천구간 보기, 'view the recommended range for your own spec') and a Korean node-type colour legend, i.e. it is a screenshot of a Korean HEXA calculator, not original English analysis. No public Demon Avenger class document exists to cross-check against: the maplestorywiki community class-guide index lists Demon Avenger with a blank entry, and the Grandis page's Other Resources block links only maplestorywiki, NamuWiki and the class Discord - no Class Doc.

hyperStats.orderingNote: DO NOT FLATTEN THIS INTO A RANKED ARRAY. NamuWiki is the only source on earth that discusses Demon Avenger hyper stats, and it presents its six stats as a descriptive list, not a ranking. It states exactly three ordering facts and no others: Damage is the number-one hyper stat for every class and Demon Avenger is no exception; Critical Rate is 'no longer essential' since the class's base crit rate was raised to 40%, and should be dropped in favour of something else if Legion occupation, Legion artifact or inner ability can cover the gap; and Max HP % is taken slowly, only after the essential hyper stats are finished. The four stats in between are each given a reason but are never ranked against one another. A previous version of this file shipped a flat ordered array (Damage, Boss Damage, Ignore DEF, Critical Damage, Critical Rate, Max HP %) whose sequence matched neither the source's own list order nor any ranking the source states - downstream code reading array position as priority would have invented a claim. That array is replaced by the tiers below.
hyperStats.sourceListOrderNote: The literal order the six stats appear in on the NamuWiki page. Recorded only so a future reader can see that it is NOT the order this file previously shipped, and so nobody mistakes it for a ranking. NamuWiki gives no indication that its list order means anything.

SEPARATELY, in its Legion section, the same page states that Demon Avenger's base critical damage of 8% is the lowest figure in the entire warrior job group and that, unlike critical rate, critical damage has limited sources, so it must be secured everywhere it can be. That is the stronger argument, but it is made about the Legion board, not about hyper stats - an earlier version of this file presented it as the hyper stat entry's own reasoning. The +8% figure itself is independently confirmed by maplestorywiki's skill data (Advanced Desperado Mastery) and by Grandis' derived-stat table.

This is the one stat the source explicitly places last.

hyperStats.notes: Grandis Library publishes no hyper stat section for any class - confirmed by re-reading the raw page data on 2026-09-12, which contains no hyperStat field - and no other GMS-side Demon Avenger source publishes one either, so the whole of the above rests on one KMS community wiki. The community's operative answer to hyper stat allocation is not a fixed list at all but a per-character optimisation against a chosen boss, computed from your own stat sheet: MathBro's hyper stat optimizer at https://brendonmay.github.io/hyperCalculator/ . Any static list, this one included, is a simplification. Where Max HP % sits is likely to move more for Demon Avenger than for a normal class, because for this class it is a main-stat line rather than a survivability line - but note that the source is aware of exactly that and still puts it last.

classSpecific.claim: The damage-to-abnormal-status line is worth more on Demon Avenger than on a generic class. NamuWiki's reason: between the Explorer mage link skill Empirical Knowledge and 'Demon Avenger's own defence-reduction debuff', the line is effectively just extra boss damage.
classSpecific.corrections: Two things in the earlier version of this claim were wrong and have been fixed. (1) It said the Explorer mage link skill 'applies a status'. It does not. maplestorywiki's GMS text for Empirical Knowledge describes a passive that, on attacking, has a chance to identify the weakness of the struck enemy with the highest Max HP and then grants the PLAYER stacking Damage and Enemy DEF Ignored against that enemy - it applies no abnormal status to anything. The half of NamuWiki's reasoning that rests on Empirical Knowledge is therefore NOT confirmed on the GMS side and may be a KMS-side or terminology artefact. (2) It named Nether Slice as the defence-reduction debuff. NamuWiki does not name any skill; it says only 'Demon Avenger's own defence-reduction debuff'. Nether Slice is this file's identification, not the source's - though it is a well-founded one: maplestorywiki's Nether Slice entry reads 'Any enemies hit will receive a debuff which temporarily reduces their defense rate', with Enemy Defense -x% for 2x seconds.

The +40% figure is independently confirmed by maplestorywiki's skill data and by Grandis' derived-stat table, which both decompose it identically as 5% base + 15% Demonic Veracity + 20% Abyssal Connection.

innerAbility.notes: Grandis splits its recommendation by the attack-speed cap of your region rather than naming GMS explicitly, and it does not state which bracket GMS falls into - confirmed by re-reading the raw page data, where the preset names are literally 'Regions w/ AS10 Cap' and 'Regions w/ AS8 Cap'. Confirm your own cap before using the attack-speed line: Grandis' own derived-stat table puts Demon Avenger at attack speed 7 (Stage 4 base, +2 from Agile Demon, +1 from Overwhelming Power), so whether a further +1 from inner ability does anything depends entirely on where the cap sits. This matters in money terms, because picking the wrong preset wastes a legendary line. Note also that NamuWiki, which is written for KMS, has no attack-speed line in any of its presets.

gearingNotes:
Demon Avenger is the class where generic gearing advice breaks down hardest, and almost every divergence traces to one skill.

BLOOD PACT (beginner skill) converts Max HP into attack power, lets Demon Avenger ignore the stat requirements on Warrior and Demon Avenger equipment, and - the part that matters most - states explicitly that only a set percentage of bonus HP from equipment is applied, and that base HP produces more damage range than HP granted by equipment and items. HP from gear is therefore NOT interchangeable with HP from levels and AP, and you cannot reason about %HP the way a STR class reasons about %STR. Source: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Avenger/Skills

STAR FORCE CONVERSION (beginner skill) turns the Star Force on your equipped items into additional Max HP, counting up to 410 stars; Star Force on medals and titles is excluded, as are guild-skill Star Force increases. Because Max HP is the damage stat, star-forcing raises Demon Avenger's main stat through a second channel that does not exist for other classes. Source: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Avenger/Skills

POTENTIAL AND BONUS POTENTIAL: %All Stat lines are close to worthless here; what you want is flat Max HP alongside some attack. On the bonus-potential (additional option) side the flat Max HP line scales with item level, at roughly item level x 21 / 18 / 15 / 12 / 9 for the top five tiers, so a level-150 armour's best HP bonus line is around 3,150 HP. On the main potential side %Max HP is the equivalent of %main stat, and because a Demon Avenger can stack several %HP lines on the same item the early cube tiers are cheaper for this class than for a stat class. Source: https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EB%AA%AC%20%EC%96%B4%EB%B2%A4%EC%A0%B8 (KMS-side; the economics are region-specific, the stat logic is not).

FLAMES are more expensive for Demon Avenger than for other classes, because the top tier of the Max HP flame line is what it needs and that forces it onto the rarer high-grade rebirth flames rather than the common ones most classes use outside their weapon. Source: https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EB%AA%AC%20%EC%96%B4%EB%B2%A4%EC%A0%B8 (KMS; flame item names differ by region, so verify the GMS equivalent before acting on it).

CRIT RATE: Demon Avenger arrives at +40% critical rate from passives alone - 5% base, +15% from Demonic Veracity and +20% from Abyssal Connection - which is enough that a crit rate inner ability or hyper stat line becomes a swap candidate rather than a requirement, but is NOT enough to reach the cap by itself. Sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Avenger/Skills and https://grandislibrary.com/resistance/demon-avenger

CRIT DAMAGE is the mirror image: the kit supplies only +8% (Advanced Desperado Mastery), described on NamuWiki as the lowest of the warrior classes, and crit damage has few sources - so crit damage from Legion, hyper stats and gear is worth more on Demon Avenger than the usual rule of thumb suggests. Sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Avenger/Skills , https://grandislibrary.com/resistance/demon-avenger , https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EB%AA%AC%20%EC%96%B4%EB%B2%A4%EC%A0%B8

BOSS DAMAGE from skills is 0%. The class's own Legion effect supplies boss damage; everything else has to come from gear, hyper stats and inner ability. Source: https://grandislibrary.com/resistance/demon-avenger

LEGION BOARD: NamuWiki singles out flat and percentage Max HP Legion members as unusually valuable for Demon Avenger, since they raise the main stat directly and the class has few other things it needs from Legion - it names Mikhail (flat Max HP) and Dark Knight (%Max HP) among them. It also names Marksman and Night Lord for critical rate, Shade for critical damage (because of the crit-damage shortage above), and Mercedes for cooldown reduction, on the grounds that the hyper, 5th and 6th job skills Demon Avenger depends on are not affected by cooldown-reset effects. One further flat-HP Legion member is named in that source but its name did not survive translation legibly, so it is omitted here rather than guessed. Source: https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EB%8D%B0%EB%AA%AC%20%EC%96%B4%EB%B2%A4%EC%A0%B8 (KMS; confirm before acting).

RESOURCE MODEL: there is no MP. HP is both the health pool and the resource, spent by nearly every skill and refunded by Life Sap / Advanced Life Sap on hit. Overload, the stacking debuff that Exceed skills apply, reduces how much Life Sap restores; Overload Release clears it in exchange for HP restoration and a final damage buff. Limits Surpassed temporarily makes skills free. Sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Demon_Avenger/Skills and https://grandislibrary.com/resistance/demon-avenger

WEAPON: multiplier 1.3x, Desperado as primary and the Demon Aegis force shield as secondary. Source: https://grandislibrary.com/resistance/demon-avenger

DELIBERATELY OMITTED: specific pendant, soul and armour-set recommendations. NamuWiki gives concrete picks, but they are written for the KMS item pool and naming, and translating them into GMS Heroic equivalents would be a guess.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating HP from equipment as equivalent to base HP when comparing gear.
commonMistakes.why: Blood Pact's own description states that only a set percentage of bonus HP from equipment is applied, and that base HP yields a greater damage range than HP from equipment and items.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling or keeping %All Stat bonus potential lines.
commonMistakes.why: All-stat percentage does essentially nothing for a class whose damage comes from Max HP; flat Max HP with some attack is the target instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Deprioritising the Chance to Skip Cooldown inner ability line.
commonMistakes.why: Every bossing preset found for this class includes it, and the KMS-side source treats the legendary 20% version as effectively mandatory for a main character because of how much of the class's damage sits behind cooldowns.

commonMistakes.mistake: Building boost nodes from maplestorywiki's Enhancement Core grouping table.
commonMistakes.why: That table lists a 'Demon Cry Boost' in its third core group; 'Demon Cry' appears exactly once on the entire Demon Avenger skills page - inside that grouping - and matches no Demon Avenger skill anywhere else on the page. The same table also omits Exceed: Double Slash Boost from every group even though it appears in the page's own final-damage table. Use the post-v.269 grouping published by Grandis Library instead, and note that Grandis exposes a separate pre-v.269 view, which is evidence the groupings changed at that patch.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating the two 6th-job infographics as two independent opinions.
commonMistakes.why: They are the Fragments-constrained and Energy-constrained outputs of the same analysis, both credited to the same Demon Avenger Discord and dated the same day, and the Energy one is visibly a screenshot of a Korean-language HEXA calculator UI.

coverageWarnings: Demon Avenger has NO public class guide document. The maplestorywiki class-guide index lists the class with a blank link, and Grandis Library links no Class Doc for it - its Other Resources block was re-read on 2026-09-12 and lists only maplestorywiki, NamuWiki and the class Discord. Every judgement field on Grandis is credited to the Demon Avenger Discord, which is not machine-readable, so the class Discord is an unaudited single point of failure for all GMS-side advice about this class. This is why no endgame claim in this file is labelled strong.

The HEXA order is transcribed from an icon infographic, not from prose. It has now been read independently by two readers who agree on all 30 transcribed steps, and node identities were fixed by pixel comparison against Grandis' own named icon files rather than by eye - but only 30 of the chart's 167 steps are transcribed, and the chart itself remains a single source.

The 'Energy Efficient' infographic is a Korean calculator screenshot - re-confirmed on 2026-09-12 by opening the image, which carries a Korean checkbox header and a Korean node-type colour legend. This strongly suggests Demon Avenger's public HEXA order is a KMS-balance calculator output relayed by the Discord rather than GMS Heroic analysis.

Hyper stat priority rests entirely on one KMS-side source, which does not actually rank most of the stats it names. This file now stores the source's three explicit ordering statements and refuses to invent the rest; MathBro's optimizer is the better answer and is linked.

NamuWiki was unreachable directly during this pass - both en.namu.wiki and namu.wiki return Cloudflare challenges to every fetch method available here. It was re-read through the namu.moe mirror of the same document, which is the same source and is counted once, not twice. The mirror's text was verified to carry the same section numbering (5.4.2 어빌리티, 5.4.3 메이플 유니온, 5.4.4 하이퍼 스탯) that this file's earlier extraction relied on.
Reddit was not reachable in this environment, so r/Maplestory Demon Avenger threads are entirely unexamined.
No YouTube guide descriptions were checked.

contest.method: Resolution pass scoped to the five endgame sections (vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility). NOTE ON STARTING STATE: this file arrived with NO contest block and no recorded defects, and demon-avenger does not appear in _contest-summary.json's filesBlocked list - so the adversarial wave recorded zero defects here and there was nothing to litigate. Rather than declare the file clean on that basis, every endgame claim was re-opened against its own cited page and checked literally. The defects below were found by this pass, not inherited.

resolved.defect: vMatrix: the claim that Grandis Library labels the two skill sets 'Primary Trio' and 'Secondary Trio', and the claim that Grandis states you should max the primary category first.
resolved.detail: Both strings are literally present in the Grandis page payload. nodeInfo.recommended.nodes reads [["Primary Trio", ...Exceed: Execution, Nether Shield, Infernal Exceed], ["Secondary Trio", ...Exceed: Lunar Slash, Thousand Swords, Bat Swarm]], and nodeInfo.recommended.notes[0] reads 'Any combination of these skills are good but preferred from same category as you want to max primary first'. Worth recording that a summarising fetch of the same URL reported the opposite - that no trio labels existed and that the mechanical notes were absent from the page. Had that summary been trusted, this pass would have deleted four correct claims. The raw payload is the authority.

resolved.defect: vMatrix: the trio membership, independently attributed to mystyjl.
resolved.detail: mystyjl's Demon Avenger block reads Bossing = Execution / Nether Shield / Infernal Exceed and Extra = Lunar Slash / Bat Swarm / Thousand Swords. Identical membership to Grandis on both sets, and the file's characterisation of the label difference ('Extra' rather than a formal second trio) is accurate. Genuine two-lineage corroboration; consensus moderate is the right label.

resolved.defect: vMatrix: the six boost node groupings and the three mechanical notes.
resolved.detail: All six groupings match the page exactly, as do all three notes and the boost-node level cap of 60 on maplestorywiki. ADDED from the same payload: Grandis marks nodes 1-4 primary and nodes 5-6 other, and assigns NO node to the Secondary category on this class, even though its generic legend mentions Secondary. That distinction was missing and is easy to confuse with the 'Secondary Trio' label, so it is now spelled out.

resolved.defect: vMatrix SHAPE: trios[].skills and boostNodeGroupings.groups were ordered arrays, but Grandis explicitly says 'any combination of these skills are good'. Array position implied a within-trio ranking the source disclaims.
resolved.detail: Added skillsOrdered:false to both trios and ordered:false to the node groupings, plus priorityOrdered:true with a note - because the ordering BETWEEN primary and secondary IS stated by the source ('max primary first') even though the ordering WITHIN a trio is not. The two cases needed different flags rather than one blanket one.

resolved.defect: hexa.order: 30 steps transcribed from an image by a single reader, which the file itself flagged as needing re-verification before being shown to a paying user.
resolved.detail: The PNG was downloaded and re-read at 6x-9x magnification by a second reader with no access to the original transcription's reasoning. All 30 steps matched exactly on all three attributes: node identity, target-level badge and node-type border colour. Node identities were not eyeballed - they were fixed by comparison against the icon files Grandis serves for this class. The node-type colour legend was verified against the companion image, which reads 마스터리 코어 purple / 스킬 코어 gold / 강화 코어 blue / 공용 코어 green. Consensus stays WEAK: double-reading fixes transcription risk, not source risk, and the source is still one Discord-relayed chart.

resolved.defect: hexa: the chart's length was given as 'roughly 165' steps.
resolved.detail: Counted from the image: 11 rows of 15 cells plus a final row of 2 = 167 steps. Changed to 167 and moved into a structured totalStepsInChart field.

resolved.defect: hexa: the file stated that the first 30 steps contain no Skill core, but gave no indication where the first one actually is.
resolved.detail: The no-Skill-core-in-the-first-30 claim is correct. Added the verifiable next fact: the first Skill core is Rageborne Devil (Ascent) to Lv 1 at step 32, read off a gold-bordered cell carrying the rageborne-devil icon, with maplestorywiki independently confirming Rageborne Devil as Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent). Steps 31-45 were NOT added wholesale, because two level badges in that row could not be read with confidence and a partially-guessed sequence is worse than a stated gap.

resolved.defect: hexa.nodeInventory: twelve HEXA core names, single-sourced to maplestorywiki.
resolved.detail: All twelve names exist verbatim on the page - no extraction artifacts of the Bow Master "Extra Quiver Cartridge" kind. Requiem is Skill Node/Core 1 (Origin) and Rageborne Devil is Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent), exactly as the file had them. ADDED: the Mastery core slot groupings (Core 1 Nether Shield; Core 2 Exceed: Execution; Core 3 Exceed: Lunar Slash + Maximal Exceed; Core 4 Thousand Swords + Infernal Exceed), which were on the page and had not been captured. Also added ordered:false, since an inventory is not a priority list.

resolved.defect: hexa: the HEXA mechanics sentence about enhancement scaling and V-skill requirements.
resolved.detail: Traced to its actual origin, Template:HEXA Skill Description, and quoted verbatim. The four Demon Avenger enhancement formulas on the skills page read 10+x+5*log10(x)+5*log20(x)+10*log30(x), which is exactly the linear-with-jumps-at-10/20/30 shape the template describes. The template is now cited alongside the skills page and explicitly marked as the same lineage, not a second source.

resolved.defect: hyperStats SHAPE - the most damaging defect in this file. hyperStats.priority shipped as an ORDERED array (Damage, Boss Damage, Ignore DEF, Critical Damage, Critical Rate, Max HP %) while its own notes conceded the section rested on a single source. Downstream code reads array position as priority.
resolved.detail: Re-read NamuWiki section 5.4.4 in the original Korean. It presents six stats as a descriptive list and states exactly three ordering facts: Damage is the number-one hyper stat for every class; Critical Rate is 'no longer essential' since base crit rate became 40% and should be dropped if Legion, artifact or inner ability can cover the gap; Max HP % is taken slowly after the essential stats are done. The four in between are never ranked against each other. Worse, the source's own list order is Damage, Critical Rate, Boss Damage, Ignore DEF, Critical Damage, HP% - so the file had silently moved Critical Rate down three places AND invented a ranking among Boss Damage, Ignore DEF and Critical Damage. Replaced the flat array with four tiers carrying explicit ordered flags: tier 1 Damage (ordered, stated), tier 2 Boss Damage + Ignore DEF + Critical Damage (ordered:false), tier 3 Critical Rate (conditional), tier 4 Max HP % (last). The source's literal list order is recorded separately and explicitly labelled as not a ranking.

resolved.defect: hyperStats CITATION INVERSION: the Critical Damage entry justified its placement with '+8% is the lowest of the warrior classes and crit damage has few other sources', attributing that reasoning to a hyper stat discussion that does not contain it.
resolved.detail: The argument is real and it is on NamuWiki - but in section 5.4.3, the Legion board section, as the reason to take Shade: Demon Avenger's base critical damage of 8% is the lowest figure in the entire warrior job group, and unlike critical rate, critical damage has limited sources. NamuWiki's actual hyper stat entry for Critical Damage says something much weaker: efficiency is very good as long as guaranteed critical is secured, and its enhancement priority past level 10 is high. Both statements are now given, each attributed to the section it actually comes from. This is the same failure mode the brief names - using text from elsewhere to raise a recommendation's apparent support.

resolved.defect: hyperStats: the Damage, Boss Damage, Ignore DEF, Critical Rate and Max HP % entries.
resolved.detail: Each was re-read in Korean and each matches. Damage: '모든 직업의 1순위 하이퍼 스탯. 데벤져도 예외는 아니다.' Boss Damage: base 0% excluding the class's own Legion effect, and worth taking even allowing for damage options that sum with it. Ignore DEF: as ignore-DEF nears 90% each 1% matters hugely, especially against bosses carrying 300% base defence - that 300% specific was missing and has been added. Critical Rate and Max HP % match as written.

resolved.defect: hyperSkills.passives: the claim that five picks 'match the five hyper passive points a character has by Lv 190', used to argue the list is a complete build rather than a ranking.
resolved.detail: No source cited in this file states how many hyper passive points a character has, and none reachable here does either - maplestorywiki has a Hyper Stats page with a full point table but no equivalent for hyper skill points. The claim was load-bearing for a structural conclusion, so hedging it was not an option. It is deleted outright. The conclusion it supported survives on better footing: Grandis itself stores the recommendation as a two-bullet build string with no ordering, so ordered:false is now justified by the source rather than by an arithmetic claim nobody can check.

resolved.defect: hyperSkills.passives: the five recommended passives and the four skipped ones.
resolved.detail: Grandis' hyperBuild.recommended reads 'Exceed - Reinforce, Reduce Overload, and Opportunity' and 'Nether Shield - Reinforce and Spread' - exactly the five. The nine available passives, their effects and their level requirements were read from the page's own hyperPassive data and match maplestorywiki; the full table is now stored rather than described in prose, so a player can see what is being skipped and why. Added ordered:false and a note that sourceCount 1 attaches to the recommendation, not to the name/level data.

resolved.defect: hyperSkills.actives: labelled consensus 'strong' on the strength of two sources. The file's own rule is that strong requires 3+ independent sources.
resolved.detail: Downgraded to moderate with sourceCount 2. The underlying facts are all correct and were re-confirmed - Forbidden Contract Lv 140, Thousand Swords Lv 160, Demonic Fortitude Lv 190, on both Grandis and maplestorywiki - and the full effect strings have been added. But no third source discusses Demon Avenger hyper actives, so 'strong' overstated it. This is precisely the mislabel the brief warns poisons the comparison feature.

resolved.defect: innerAbility: the three Grandis presets, verbatim.
resolved.detail: All three match the raw payload exactly, including the preset names 'Regions w/ AS10 Cap' and 'Regions w/ AS8 Cap' and the training note 'Depending on what's chosen as the 1st Line, choose the other for the 2nd Line'. The file's observation that Grandis never maps a cap to a region name is correct.

resolved.defect: innerAbility: the AS8 bossing preset labelled moderate on the strength of NamuWiki independently arriving at the same three lines.
resolved.detail: NamuWiki's boss-specialised preset reads 재사용 / 보공 / 상추 - cooldown skip, boss damage, abnormal-status damage - in that order, described as the endgame preset for a character whose fundamentals are in place. Same three lines, same order, same tiers (legendary 20 / unique 10 / unique 8). This is a real two-lineage agreement and moderate is correct. Also ADDED a NamuWiki bossing variant that this file had missed entirely: 재사용 / 보공(or상추) / 크확, for a character short on critical rate.

resolved.defect: innerAbility.training: labelled 'moderate - Grandis Library and NamuWiki agree on the meso/drop pair', which glossed over the third line.
resolved.detail: The meso/drop tiebreak the file credits to NamuWiki is exactly right and was re-read verbatim: take Meso Obtained on the top line because it is hard to source elsewhere and applies multiplicatively with meso-farming consumables, then secure Item Drop Rate. But the third line is a REAL DISAGREEMENT that went unrecorded: Grandis says Chance to Skip Cooldown +10%, NamuWiki says damage to normal monsters and argues against cooldown skip while hunting because mobs evaporate before a reset is worth anything. The third line is now left unfilled and marked CONTESTED, a new conflicts entry records it, and the consensus label is explicitly scoped to lines 1 and 2 only.

resolved.defect: innerAbility.classSpecific: the claim that 'the Explorer mage link skill applies a status as well', used to argue the abnormal-status condition is close to always-on.
resolved.detail: Checked the cited mechanic independently. maplestorywiki's Empirical Knowledge entry describes a passive that, on attacking, has a chance to identify the weakness of the struck enemy with the highest Max HP and then grants the PLAYER stacking Damage and Enemy DEF Ignored against that enemy. It applies no abnormal status to anything. NamuWiki does invoke Empirical Knowledge in its reasoning, so the file relayed the source faithfully - but the paraphrase 'applies a status' is the file's own and it is wrong. The claim is retained as NamuWiki's, with the failed GMS-side check recorded beside it and consensus dropped to weak.

resolved.defect: innerAbility.classSpecific: the abnormal-status claim named Nether Slice as the defence-reduction debuff and cited NamuWiki for it.
resolved.detail: NamuWiki names no skill - it says only '데벤의 자체 방깎 디버프', Demon Avenger's own defence-reduction debuff. Nether Slice is this file's identification. It is a good one: maplestorywiki's Nether Slice entry reads 'Any enemies hit will receive a debuff which temporarily reduces their defense rate', with Enemy Defense -x% for 2x seconds. But the attribution is now stated as the file's inference rather than the source's assertion.

resolved.defect: innerAbility.classSpecific: the strong cooldown-skip claim, including 'a player who cannot get this line should reconsider maining the class'.
resolved.detail: Re-read in Korean and it is, if anything, understated in the file. NamuWiki calls the line '1순위 고정' - fixed as first priority - ties it to Shield Chasing uptime (실드 체이싱, which is Nether Shield in GMS naming, so the file's mapping is right), notes the Legion artifact is brought on top of it, and then says outright that without this ability you should reconsider making Demon Avenger your main.

resolved.defect: innerAbility.classSpecific: the Critical Rate swap-candidate claim.
resolved.detail: NamuWiki: crit rate is 40%, not that low but not high either; if Legion occupation, the Legion artifact and so on can supply enough, replace the line with boss damage or abnormal-status damage. The +40% decomposition (5% base + 15% Demonic Veracity + 20% Abyssal Connection) is confirmed identically on maplestorywiki and Grandis, so sourceCount 3 on the figure - but the judgement itself is still single-source, and the consensusWhy now says which is which.

outOfScope: gearingNotes in its entirety - Blood Pact and Star Force Conversion mechanics, potential and bonus-potential guidance, flame economics, the Legion board picks, the resource model, the weapon multiplier and the deliberately-omitted item recommendations. Not one of the five endgame sections named in the brief, so it was left untouched. Incidentally, several of its claims were confirmed in passing while reading the same pages for in-scope work - the Legion picks (Mikhail and Soul Master and Lethe for flat HP, Dark Knight for %HP, Marksman and Night Lord for crit rate, Shade for crit damage, Mercedes for cooldown reduction with the stated reason that hyper, 5th and 6th job skills do not benefit from cooldown-skip effects), the crit rate and crit damage decompositions, and Boss Damage 0% all check out.
